g.text: CONTRACT, NOT RTL. The R3 debug-control contract is frozen (manager ruling
exists, but pe_ctrl.v and pe_cpu.v contain no bp_ or step signal — only
comments about what a debugger would need. This section is red on purpose.
The two levers that move it: the bp comparator plus debug response mux, and
STOP-BEFORE semantics so a breakpoint lands before the matched instruction
The architectural point of the whole firmware-protocols effort: these are not
peripherals. They are PROGRAMS on the same CPU, pin matrix and tick, which is
why a rate the tick cannot express (MIDI 31.25 kbaud, DMX 250 kbaud) is
still reachable — by counting instructions. Measured on the pin: MIDI
31,998.7 ns / 31,251 baud and DMX 3,999.8 ns / 250,010 baud, both with zero
THE REMAINING RED. Everything above is simulated and mapped; the physical
Pico/USB board acceptance is the one item no simulation can close.
Baseline firmware personas: UART, SPI master, I2C master.
The passive loader is a separate SPI path used to load instruction SRAM.
Current aliases: uo_out[0] is UART TX / SPI SCLK; ui_in[0] is UART RX /
SPI MISO; uio[0:1] are I2C SDA/SCL; uio[2:3] are SPI MOSI/CS_N.
ui_in[2] is 10BASE-T RX; uo_out[2] is 10BASE-T TX (G6 reclaim of dbg_pc[0]).
The Linux GUI and its PC-to-board transport are planned software; the
transport and control API are not chosen yet. The RP2040 sits on the Tiny
Tapeout demo board and is the chip-side SPI host.
Landed 2026-09-24 (manager decision): the R1 framed host bus supersedes the
A1 raw uio[4] echo — SPI mode 0, MSB-first 16-bit words, 16'hA55A sync,
CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE, response opcode bit 7, sequence/target echoed; the
commit-latched word echo lives in the framed LOAD response. Pads: uio[4:7]
CS_N/MOSI/MISO/SCK, uo_out[1] = IRQ_N (sticky, active low), ui_in[3:5]
freed; 19 of 24 committed. See wiki/plans/host-controller-gui.md and
Landed 2026-09-24: ONE pe_serdes with split payload-only enables (TX
advances only on payload cells, serdes.tx_bit_en = tx_codec_cell_en &&
!tx_stuffed; RX captures only payload cells, serdes.rx_bit_en =
rx_codec_cell_en && rx_bit_valid). TWO unmodified pe_codec_mux instances are
independent 2x half-cell LEVEL; the pad overlay sits before the matrix's
open-drain gate, and a latched-phase window on port 0xF has
separate TXLEN/RXLEN. First consumer is the wire loopback (plain and stuffed
Manchester, word 0x07E0) through TX codec, simulation wire model, DRU/codec
RX, and SERDES RX; a trailing stuff cell is covered by construction. The
10BASE-T TX frame consumer (pe_eth_tx) is integrated below and shares the
TX codec through the tx_path owner mux. Landed 2026-09-25 (plan Tasks 1-5):
full frame from firmware pushes, 32-entry window, owner mux, G6 uo_out[2]
pad, loopback acceptance PASS (FCS 9cc5cb34, IFG 102 cells). Plan Tasks 6
Low-speed USB and CAN are later personas; JTAG, SWD, and PS/2 are optional.
A1 word echo; one frame late
board connections, including optional SPI MISO
